result_text:
The `all_files.zip` export now looks up each scope file list by its configured aspect name, so renaming `buildAndDeployment` no longer breaks the export. I did not run the renamed-aspect scenario end to end, and no existing test covers `exportJson`.

**What was wrong:** the five zip entries used fixed file names such as `aspect_build_and_deployment.txt`. When the aspect was renamed, the file on disk was `aspect_buildAndDeployment.txt`, so the read threw. The surrounding `try` caught the exception and printed a stack trace, which skipped the rest of the block including `git-history.zip`.

**What I changed**, in `reports/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/reports/dataexporters/DataExporter.java`:
- In `exportJson`, the five literal entries of `all_files.zip` are now calls to a new helper, `getAspectTextEntry(aspect)`, passed in the same order: main, test, generated, build and deployment, other.
- The new private helper derives the file name with `DataExportUtils.getAspectFileListFileName(aspect, "")`. That is the same function that writes the loose `aspect_<name>.txt` files, so the two cannot drift apart. It then reads the file and returns the name and content pair.

With the default configuration the entry names are unchanged. With `buildAndDeployment` the fourth entry becomes `aspect_buildAndDeployment.txt`.

`mvn -q -o -pl reports test` ran without errors. I did not run `mvn install` and did not commit.
